utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In response to Your Honours' question number 1, who were the perpetrators of the alleged killings of Milenko Stanic and Zivinko Todorovic, the prosecution submits that the perpetrators were members of the El Mujahid Detachment, which was operation in joint combat with units of the ARBiH in and around the Kesten area at the time of the capture. The combination of the testimony of the three women describing the mixture of regular ARBiH soldiers and "Mujahedin in the group," the combat orders and maps showing the joint combat, and the El Mujahid Detachment being a key unit in the operation and being present in the area on the 11th of September, all of which will be covered in more detail by my colleague Mr. Neuner, and the events that followed the capture, which I will be covering in some detail, all of this evidence together, with the lack of any credible evidence disputing that it was the El Mujahid Detachment, leads to only one reasonable inference that can be drawn, and that is that the El Mujahid Detachment were present during the capture and killed those two persons. The Prosecution further submits, however, that if the Chamber were to find otherwise with respect to the identity of the perpetrators who killed Milenko Stanic and Zivinko Todorovic, this finding would not affect the Prosecution's case with regard to the two groups of POWs, the 51 and the ten, and the three women who were taken from the hall in Kesten by the El Mujahid Detachment to their camp in Kamenica and subjected to cruel treatment and some of them murdered. What is important is the identity of the group that seized the prisoners from Kesten. And the Prosecution submits that this evidence, the evidence shows beyond a reasonable doubt, that it was the El Mujahid Detachment that took those prisoners and women from the hall in Kesten. I will now proceed with the presentation on the points raised in the Defence brief with regard to the September crime base. By reading of the Defence brief indicates that they raise -- they dispute four points. Defence states the EMD did not take over the prisoners from the 5th Battalion at Kesten; the Defence states that the EMD did not take control of the three women; Defence asserts that neither the women nor the VRS soldiers, the 51, were taken to the Kamenica camp; the Defence asserts that the women were held by an unknown group for the first two days of their detention; and, finally, the Defence asserts that the identity of remains of bodies found in the Kamenica grave has not been proven. As I will discuss the evidence, each of the assertions, it will become clear that each of these assertions have no basis in fact. The first assertion, in paragraph 5577 of the Defence brief, Defence states that no other witness testified as to the death of Zivinko Todorovic. So the Prosecution has failed to prove that somebody of that identity was killed. This assertion is not correct. As Your Honours will recall, Mr. Krcmar testified that he had spent the last several years at the RS office for missing persons, an organisation whose goal it was to find these persons as a result of these operations, and that he spent several years doing that. This slide shows the witness, Mr. Krcmar, testified about Exhibit 652. This is the card of the missing person issued by his office. The name of the person is Zivinko Todorovic, as you can see from the card. The next slide is the excerpt of the testimony of Mr. Krcmar, where he says this is the report of the identification of mortal remains for Zivinko Todorovic. And we can see the signatures of the members of the family and persons competent for the identification, all their signatures. Now this is B/C/S, but the next slide has the English version. And this is the first page, and the second page has the name, Zivinko Todorovic. And as will be discussed later, this is the final document in the procedural stage of identifying victims. But if that isn't enough to prove that the Defence is wrong in asserting that no other witness has testified about the death of Zivinko Todorovic, I'd like to show you the next slide in closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Next, at paragraph 588, the Defence asserts that the Prosecution has failed to prove on the evidence that the persons seizing the 52 POWs were members of the EMD. As Your Honours have heard the testimony, and as we explained in detail in our final trial brief: "The Prosecution has proved beyond a reasonable doubt that the VRS soldiers, along with a few women and children, surrendered in groups in the upper part of Kesten near a creek, to the 2nd Company of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Mountain Brigade. One such group of Serbs was captured in the forests in the afternoon of 11 September 1995 by ARBiH soldiers, including the EMD, and they were led to Kesten." Exhibit 466, which I will show you in full in the next two slides, the commander of the 35th Division confirmed that he issued an order to the EMD at midnight on the 10th of September, instructing that part of the forces of the EMD be kept for intervention in the sector of Kesten village. The EMD were in Kesten village on the 11th of September. This is the front page of that order, and the next slide is the quotation from the order as I just read. Now, another key document that rebuts the Defence assertion that the EMD did not take the POW is the regular daily combat report of the 328th Brigade, dated 13 September 1995. This report says: "On 11 September 1995, two companies of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade captured 61 hostiles and three Serbian women in the Kesten village sector. Members of the El Mujahid unit took charge of all the captives except two, while the two were turned over to the 328th Brigade military police." Now, you've heard from witnesses, especially Mr. Karahasanovic, that he couldn't confirm -- this slide is the B/C/S version of the document. Mr. Karahasanovic would not commit that this was the same group of POWs, but I would suggest that that is preposterous. This group talks about 61 hostiles - and we'll look at the list in a bit - three women, and then the release of two, which, as you recall, were two minorities that were released. There is simply too much coincidently to have this to be not the same group. The report could not be any clearer that it was the EMD who took over those prisoners at Kesten. The next three slides are under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now paragraph 76 of his statement is very significant, and it says: "When we returned to Kesten, a vehicle, Lada Niva, approached us, which was some kind of ambulance car for the 4th Manoevre Battalion. The driver was asking me for the location with the two killed soldiers. The driver of the Lada gave a message that the 1st Battalion of the 328th Brigade was to go towards Marica Vis. I gave more soldiers to that forest. Sogolj and I went back to Kesten. At that time, we saw a jeep driving through the village of Kesten coming towards us. The jeep was passing by us, and in the jeep there was sitting seven or eight Arabs. Fifty metres, the car drove on a mine, and three or four of the Arabs got killed and three got injured." I don't have to read the rest of it. The significant part is the jeep with the Arabs driving in Kesten. The next slide, which is going to relate to this, is Mr. Karahasanovic's statement which was admitted as Exhibit 1355; and, as know, he also testified. What are significant are two paragraphs in his 18 September 1996 statement, which was Exhibit 1354, and he says: "On this day, we all together had 62 prisoners. However, the two children should not be counted as prisoners, although they are included in the 62. Also, four POW taken by Arabs and the two killed should not be counted here." Now, the next paragraph is perhaps the more significant of these two: "When I was there at the hall in Kesten, a unit which was called El Mujahid came. This was a unit consisted of foreigners, and they are the same unit I spoke about previously in Livada, Kamenica, at the 13 km. where they had a camp. "13 km." means thirteen kilometres from Zavidovici along the river Gostovici. As the unit entered the hall in Kesten, the Serb soldiers were lined along the wall as I took their names. The El Mujahid started yelling, and I talked to one of them who spoke Bosnian. He told us to leave the building. I replied to him to these were soldiers who had given themselves in to us, and they were our responsibility. He then shouted, "Get out or we will kill you." He then said, "These are our prisoners. We liberated this territory. You do not have anything to do with this." The person then said, "Because of them. Our brothers got killed." Mr. Karahasanovic goes on to say: "I assume this referred to a happening the same day, one hour earlier, when one of the cars of the El Mujahid went on a mine and several of them were killed. We had already heard about this story." I think Your Honours can read the rest. So it is clear, Your Honours, from the statements that Mr. Karahasanovic can only be talking about the EMD. This is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from this statement. He describes in great detail the camp, the 13th kilometre. The only unit that had access and used that camp were the EMD. But let's stay with the evidence provided by Mr. Karahasanovic for a minute. Go back one, please. Okay. The Defence, in paragraph 587, says the Prosecution attempted to attack Mr. Karahasanovic's credibility, referring to two previous written statements; however, he explained the pressure of the OTP investigator had used in taking the statements. The Defence goes on to say: "The Trial Chamber should not attach any weight to the term used in Karahasanovic's witness statements in considering the issue of the identity of the Arabs." Now, I ask you: Is that a credible assertion? The Chamber has to ask itself: Is it credible that Mr. Karahasanovic was pressured by an OTP investigator to say certain words, or that certain words were changed and he was forced to sign his statement. The Prosecution submits that this is not reasonable. In his statements, Exhibit 1354, the term "El Mujahedin units" is used in paragraphs 25 and 26; the term "El Mujahedin" without the units, is mentioned at paragraph 27; the term "El Mujahid" is used in paragraph 51, four times; the term "El Mujahid Detachment" is used in paragraph 56; and the word "Arabs" is used in paragraphs 40, four times, and in paragraphs 47 and 49. Now the question is: If words were being put into the mouth of Mr. Karahasanovic, or he was being pressured or his statement was being changed, then all of these terms would be changed to read "El Mujahid Detachment." But it wasn't. The words were not changed. These were the words that Mr. Karahasanovic used with the investigator, and it is clear from his statements when he was talking about the El Mujahid Detachment, the EMD. In paragraph 57 of this statement, he says: "I have nothing I want to add to this statement, have no complaints about the way this statement is taken." Is it time? A few more minutes? But if this isn't enough, we go to the next slide. Back, please. Okay. Thank you. Mr. Karahasanovic states later, in a later statement, Exhibit 1355, in paragraph 51, which is the long paragraph I just read: "I wish it to be stated that the soldiers who came to the Kesten -- to the centre in Kesten were Arabs. In accordance with what I know, I think the Arabs were in the El Mujahid unit since this was the only unit in our zone of responsibility that had Arabs. Every time the El Mujahid unit is mentioned, that is related to our intelligence on the Arabs belonging to this unit. They were the only ones wearing headbands with Arabic inscriptions." Now the EMD, by this statement, it is it perfectly clear that the EMD was the only unit in his zone of responsibility that had Arabs, plain and simply. The Chamber should also consider this, as assistant commander for security for the 5th Battalion, if there was another group of Arabs operating in his zone of responsibility, he would have known that. That is just common sense. When he gave his statements and used the word "El Mujahid" and other similar words, he was referring only to the El Mujahid Detachment. And one last slide. To end this point that this was the only unit and could have been the only unit and was the only unit that took those prisoners, Mr. Karahasanovic was asked: "Are you aware of the capture of any other prisoners and three Serbian women that day by anyone in the 5th Battalion? That's a yes or no, sir." His answer was: "Not in the 5th Battalion." "Okay. Are you aware of the capture of prisoners by any other battalion on that day. And the answer is: "No." So it is simply not credible that there was any other unit in the Kesten hall on that day. Take a break?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Just a word about circumstantial evidence, because we believe that the trip to Kamenica and the killing, the murders, and the cruel treatment of the POWs and the women is, of course, all based mainly on circumstantial evidence. And the circumstantial case consists of evidence of a number of different circumstances which, taken in combination, point to the guilt of the accused, because they would usually exist in combination only because the accused did what is alleged against him. That's all you need to read at that point. That's the case here, Your Honour. All of the evidence, all of the pieces put together, can only lead to the one conclusions, and that was in this case the POWs and women were taken to the EMD camp in Kamenica. We start out with the women leaving the hall, and Witness Omerasevic said that, after he left the hall, he saw -- he turned Mujahedin and the POWs about 50 metres on the right side of the road in a field in Krcevine. When he drove through Krcevine, he saw two trucks and a jeep. Now each of the women have told their story about how they were led out of the hall in Kesten and taken to an unspecified location nearby, where each told them how they were threatened by Mujahedin, as they called them, and the soldiers of the ARBiH who protected them. The statements given by these witnesses, of course, have differences, Your Honours, but it is the differences that make them totally believable. If they were all the same, then that would be the case that the stories were contrived. But because there are these differences, the evidence is stronger that there is only one reasonable inference, and we will go into some of the evidence in a minute, to show that they were taken to Kesten with the two trucks of POWs. The next 20 slides are under seal. May we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Slide 76 and 77 show the record of identification for Savo Todorovic. That's one of the six bodies. Next page, please. There. And now rather than show you all of them, I've summarized them for you. Attached to the 92 ter statement of Mr. Krcmar are the records of identification of mortal remains for all six of those bodies, and those are the page numbers that you find the records of those remains. So, therefore, again, the Defence is wrong. Now Defence has attempted to create doubt about the identity of these bodies exhumed at the grave near Kamenica by relying on a document that has been refuted by the same entity that wrote the original document. In light of the letter, from Mr. Spaic, which is -- here is the letter, and then if you go to the next slide, I have highlighted critical part of the letter. He completely explains that when they wrote on that initial list that those bodies had been exhumed, that that was not correct. And the next one is the same. "In our opinion, the misunderstanding occurred in relation between a mistaken comprehension of terms, 'missing persons' and 'exhumed persons'." Now, this is a perfectly logical explanation and the Prosecution finds it inconceivable that the Defence continues to rely on a letter to try to cast doubt about the identity of these bodies where this letter has been completely refuted by the author of the letter. Couple of more points, Your Honour. Defence says -- challenges a photograph in which Mr. Krcmar testified about the persons in the photograph. The Defence says that Krcmar claimed that the two men depicted were Dragan Lukic and Marko Maric. However, if regard is had to the Karahasanovic list, it can be seen that the two men that Krcmar claims to have recognised are not named as persons who were taken from Kesten. Well, again, we have to say the Defence is wrong on that. Mr. Krcmar says: "On this list these two persons'" -- he said: "On the list I compiled, they appear under 5 and 46." Well, let's look at number 5. Number 5 is Lukic Dragutin. Dragutin has got the same date of birth and place of birth. You can see next to his name, number 5, you can see the missing card. Dragan and Dragutin are the same persons, Your Honour. With regard to Mr. Marko Maric, which, again, is the subject of question number 2 from Your Honours, Mr. Krcmar testified that number 46 on the list, which I will show you in a minutes, says Marko Maricic Mr. Krcmar said: "However, his name if Maric Marko," Maric being the last name, and his father's name is Marko as well. So number 46 on the list is Mirko Maricic -- excuse me, Marko Maric, not Mirko Maricic. And if you look at the date and place of birth for Marko Maric on the left side of the screen, it matches the entry for number 46.

utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio, I'm unsure of whether the entry on the right side of the screen matches the place of birth.

utterances.text: Well, I should clarify that, Your Honour. It was unclear, and I think the testimony showed -- Mr. Karahasanovic asked where they were from, where they were from, and when the witnesses answered, it could be from, they were from recently or they were born there. But Mr. Krcmar that there was known in his database by the name of Mirko Maricic, and it is his conclusion, based on his records, that the person is Marko Maric. utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Let me, first of all, state that I'm aware about the time, and I will try my best to finish within the time allotted to the Prosecution. I hope I don't need to go over. I have tried to reduce the presentation as much as possible, so let me just start right away with the questions which were asked, questions 5 and 8, as Mr. Mundis said, should be addressed by myself. Question 8 was: "Which additional criteria can be found in the evidence of the present case that should lead this Trial Chamber to infer effective control of the ARBiH over the EMD?" Your Honours, I will address effective control over the EMD. And, first of all, I can say that the Prosecution has proposed certain indicia already in paragraph 46, and I don't want to say in addition to them, but I would just, in an effort to answer Your Honours' question, try to propose maybe additional questions as sought by Your Honours. First of all, we would say it is remarkable that throughout its existence the EMD stayed within the AOR of the 3rd Corps. If it, as the Defence claims, would be just in a relationship of horizontal -- or in horizontal relationship to the 3rd Corps, why did the EMD, throughout its existence, near leave the AOR of the 3rd Corps? It engaged in combat on the battlefields of the 3rd Corps, and as Your Honours have heard, there is one instance at the Sarajevo battlefield in December 1992 where the Mujahedin from Poljanice had left, indeed, the AOR of the 3rd Corps to carry out a combat operation near Sarajevo, but our position is the very fact that the EMD always remained within the 3rd Corps indicates, in fact, that it accepted to be subordinated to that corps. A second point is - Your Honours have heard this, this morning, already - that the EMD always sought permission or authorisation before an attack. Witnesses such as Mr. Aiman have stated so. They never fought unauthorised. We have pled the third point already. Partially the pullout of wounded of the EMD during joint combat shows also a high sophistication of labour. A certain part of the troops get killed at the front line in the first echelon with the second echelon being busy pulling out the wounded. Thirdly, the training, which was also mentioned by the Prosecution in its final trial brief, where was it carried out? You have heard, Your Honours, that it was carried out at the ninth kilometre where the 4th Manoevre Battalion was stationed and it was carried out in Ozren where the 5th ManBat of the ARBiH was having its headquarter. So where is the training conducted? It is conducted in installations assigned by the ARBiH to its units. It is not conducted somewhere else in the forest, in a hidden place, where we cannot define who owns the property. It is conducted on the compound of previously assigned installations. Another indicator, Your Honours, is -- and Mr. Zilkic testified about this. There is also one order in evidence. Mr. Zilkic assigns for his 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade officers who should go with 5th Battalion troops while these troops are subordinated to the El Mujahedin Detachment. It is not they are just given away. Let the EMD decide independently on its own what is to be done. It is, rather, that officer go with them, and they have also a kind of task to look what 5th Battalion 328th Brigade soldiers are doing while being engaged with the El Mujahedin Detachment. Moving on to the next question, question 5, Your Honours asked for the Defence's position that Rasim Delic can only be held responsible under Article 7(3) if he directly commanded the unit.

utterances.text: Can you go slowly? I think Judge Lattanzi wants to say something. Yes, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the first factor, or criterion, we're talking about the AOR of the 3 K where the EMD would take place in combat operations, I do not understand how can this be an indicator allowing us to understand the effective control rather than a coordination between the army and the detachment. Could you please go back on that point, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would submit that if, assume the EMD was very independent, it could have switched the AOR -- independent of the army, or independent of the 3rd Corps, it could have switched from the 3rd Corps AOR to the 7th Corps, fight more on the Travnik side of the battlefield, for example, move then, as has happened, with the Mujahedin from Poljanice in 1992, December, would then move to the Sarajevo battlefield and thereby, through each movement, across corps boundaries, wait, being controlled by one particular corps. And this, indeed, has not happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On question number 5, returning to that question, we would reserve our position waiting for the Defence, because Your Honours addressed primarily the Defence, and if the case may be, respond to whatever the Defence will submit to Your Honours. I would now focus on five rebuttal points relating to the command and control section of the Defence, and the first one is whether the EMD reported to the ARBiH. And you can see here in paragraph 912 that the Defence says: "The EMD did not submit military reports to its alleged superior commands, the 35th Division or 3rd Corps ..." We would say, if we talk about written reports, we do not necessarily agree; but our focus is there were a significant number of oral reports, and I'm going to cover these oral reports in a minute. So the reporting about military matters we are talking about is in fact an oral -- is an oral reporting which occurred frequently. And we have developed a system for Your Honours that, first, we have meetings on the highest 3rd Corps level, where instructions are given, transfer to certain AORs and so forth, so the EMD shows up at the 3rd Corps and gets a new mission, a new objective, transfer to another battlefield. The second point then would be on a lower level we have, again, the oral reporting or the meetings, the EMD being summoned, so after the 3rd Corps has defined the mission of the EMD, you have the OG or division carrying out subsequent meetings, and along the way, receiving also oral briefings. And, as Your Honours may see, before, during, and after combat. I start in the very early days, in 1993. We have here Mr. Hamad, stating, and it is highlighted that: In the first six months of 1993, this was the question, he met several times, Alagic he is talking about: "Sometimes he visited us in Bijelo Bucje on the eve of the attack." So before the attack. "When we were planning an attack." Next sentence: "Sometimes I would meet him in Travnik," so obviously not directly during combat, "and sometimes I would have a meeting with Mr. Alagic during the attack." He continues: "When we take over positions from the VRS or the HVO, then he would come to talk to me and to learn from me what had been done," is it is after the attack. This is transcript page 31, 7th of September, 2007. This is now a slide relating to Operation Manevar in autumn 1994. And it isn't stated -- I believe it is Aiman talking on the 8th of February, 2008, page 73, he mentions the systems of meetings. "The first meeting was a separate meeting at the corps," the highest level, as I said. And then he goes on: "Then there was an encounter at the division command, at Fadil Hasanagic's. "After that, there was one when we informed them." So somebody is reporting. "However, there were two meetings more. The last meeting was when all the commanders of other units were summoned who insisted on their readiness to execute the attack." Moving on to Proljece 1, May 1995. Hasanagic testified to Your Honours on page 3278 and 3279 on the 28th of September, 2007, "Talking about Mr. Maali, he was introduced to me as Emir of the unit." When? "When he delivered," meaning Maali, delivered the plan on the 15th of May." Your Honours will recall on the 27th of May, the combat started for Proljece 1. This is the plan, Exhibit 439, Your Honours have seen. Hasanagic testified; he made handwritten remarks on it. So what happens before Proljece 1? Again, Awad: "There were at least two meetings before the attack was carried out. The first meeting was at the 3rd Corps command, the second meeting in Zavidovici. "At the last meeting, it was decided when the attack would be launched. The particular date and hour was fixed of the attack. It may have been about two days before the attack ..." Then, during Proljece 1, what is Mr. Awad testifying. "If one of the participants in the attack were to send a message or if something had to be passed on in Bosnian, I would do that, or if somebody was speaking in Bosnian, I would interpret to the commander and pass on the orders. If it was necessary to establish connection with division command or their communication centre to ask for an artillery support ...," another indicator in the Prosecution's point of view, "then I would do so, using the Motorola that was linked to the division command." 23 This is 9th of February, page 8789. What do we have after Proljece 1? Again, Mr. Awad: "Once these three features were taken - that's the question - did the detachment report?" "Yes," Mr. Awad says, "in the evening a meeting was held at the division command." And he goes on: "Then we reported about how many casualties we had, how many killed and wounded, what else was needed in order to contain the success." I'm moving on to the next operation, Proljece 2, and here is a meeting before that operation. Again, Mr. Awad, 9th February, page 94, explained to Your Honours. He is refers to Mahmuljin: "We were told to change our direction of reconnaissance." So there was definitely a meeting with the corps commander; and later, for sure, there was one with the division command. The question was: "When was it happening?" Mr. Awad testified to Your Honours: "Definitely in late June, when the meeting was held." I'm moving to early July, 6 July 1995, now, Exhibit 602. It goes to Kakanj, and Your Honours can see what is reported about the 6th of July: "During the day, an officer team of the detachment visited the 35th Division in order to coordinate the tasks received for the upcoming combat activities." Tasks are received. Then during Proljece, Mr. Hasanagic - I have skipped this now - has also reported that for Proljece 2 the time before, the time of the operation was agreed to at the meeting. I'm talking about during Proljece 2. Again, Mr. Awad, 9th of February, 101 and 102 of the transcript: "So the question is: After the operation on 21 July, was there a meeting?" The answer is: "That was the same day or the next day, I can't say. There was a meeting and then the report would be submitted about the success of the operation." With reporting here. Your Honours have heard evidence how many times the issue of POWs had been dealt with in the July operation. I have just listed, on the left-hand side, three meetings relating to POWs; 22nd July in Livada, Fadil Imamovic testified to Your Honours, Exhibit 553; I believe on or after 24 July, Mr. Mrkajlovic and Mr. Hajderhodzic went to Livada. And Your Honours have seen here Exhibit 859 displayed on the right hand, and what does it say? "In the interview with captured aggressors soldiers, the 35th Division SVB learned the following information," and Your Honours have seen it is a lengthy description of what the interview had achieved or obtained for results than the 22nd of July 1995, document Exhibit 553. I'm moving to Farz. Meetings before Farz. Awad told Your Honours that: "The detachment commander Muatez was there, and I was present, Sakib Mahmuljin was there. We had already started preparations and were doing reconnaissance in the area." What was the meeting about? Mr. Awad told you: We were given this part of the area, Paljenik. Page 106 and 7 on the 9th of February 2008. What happened hours before Farz? We are talking at 9.00 in the evening, entry 7, on the 9th of September: The commander of the El Mujahedin, Aiman, had a meeting with the 3rd Corps commander at Luka -- excuse me, IKM 1, hours before the attack." What happens on day one of Farz -- I apologise. Maybe I start with this. This is the map a little bit modified by us in the sense that we have with a red box indicated the AOR of attack for the El Mujahedin Detachment. And, Your Honours, to show how jointly coordinated the combat was carried out, you see the El Mujahedin Detachment has neighbours, the 328th Mountain Brigade and the 329 Mountain Brigade: The 328 Mountain Brigade being upwards in the north, 329th being on the southern part. Here, Your Honours, can see roughly in Svinjasnica, the start, towards Paljenik and towards Stug. Please remember these two places. This is exhibit 76 on the right-hand side drawn by Senad Begovic. We have just recaptured for Your Honours's attention the way with these red arrows. And this is reported on day one of the operation, 10th of September, six times Mr. -- the EMD -- a member of the EMD is reporting. I think it is Awad. Begin of combat five to six. After 25 minutes the first report -- and this is the first two and a half/three hours, Your Honours. Paljenik seized at 0634, the second message from the EMD. You have just seen it on the map. Then 0800 hours, the EMD requested that Stog facility be shelled. This is what the Prosecution says: The EMD couldn't do it alone, it needed artillery support. And after Stog had been shelled, the sixth message we are talking about at 0837, they are in Stog. They have reached it. And this is what Mr. Hasanagic told Your Honours. Another meeting on that day, no longer phone or other communication, it is direct encounter. On the road, which is marked here - I think it is Exhibits 472 and 470 - Your Honours see where the arrow draws that is a direction of drive of Mr. Hasanagic and Stog, which was you have just seen shelled after 8.00 in the morning. The meeting is before Stog, Your Honours. The meeting in the evening of day one at Panorama. Your Honours have heard so much about it. I will just say something from Mr. Zilkic, who had attended along with the EMD members. What does Mr. Zilkic say to Your Honours? What was the topic of discussion, was the question. Primarily on the subsequent tasks, tomorrow's tasks. We're talking about 11 of September, Your Honours. The meetings on the 10th in the evening. What were the tasks that were discussed concerning 11 September 1995? Continuation of offensive activities. Mr. Zilkic goes on. Further advancement towards [indiscernible] feature. Your Honours have heard about this. We have displayed it on a map. The red boxes is the first combat we just talked about from roughly Svinjasnica via Paljenik to Stog. The meeting takes place at the end of first combat in the evening. The second one is Kesten [indiscernible] EMD acts as an intervention unit. The third one is the green one. The three green - I will discuss it in a moment with Your Honours - is the combat towards Koruga [phoen] discussed on that meeting. Panorama. Number 4 is also on the 11th of September. It is all in our final trial brief, Your Honours. It is Radulovo Brdo. And number 5 is almost not depicted on this map. The combat has moved north We are five days behind, around the 16th of September. The first one, Ms Sartorio has already introduced you to that combat. I don't mention it. The order was issued at midnight 10 September following meeting at IKM Panorama. As mentioned by Mr. Zilkic, a moment ago, the combat towards Koruga, takes -- or is ordered at 11.30 on the 11th of September. The prisoners in Kesten are not yet arrested or about to get arrested. And where is the EMD starting from? Djurica Vis. I don't want to say a stone-head [sic] away from Kesten, but not far away, towards north-west Koruga. The EMD complies with the order, Your Honours. The forced combat activity, Radulovo Brdo, ordered at 1730 that day, 11 September, and carried out in the Prosecution's point of view, the 5th. Okay. Then after these four subsequent combat operations, we're talking about 48 hours, Your Honours, we have is this meeting. You have heard about it. You see the participants: Number, 3 Abu Maali; number 3, Mr. Mahmuljin, as direct subordinate of Mr. Delic. Exhibit 1212. Let's move to the next. Who is the sitting on the other said of that table? Mr. Husic helped us. Number 3 is Bakir Alispahic who had, as minister of the interior, authorised Vranduk. Now he is sitting at the table together with the subject or the object of his activity. Vranduk, a joint operation against the El Mujahedin Detachment. Two months or three months after May, we are seeing a participant to this meeting. Number one, you hardly see it. It is above the head of the first person on the left-hand side. We see Mr. Ekrem Alihodzic, the former assistant commander for military security, who was at the time when Vranduk was implemented the acting or the assistant commander for military security. You see the 3rd Corps side of Operation Vranduk sitting at the same table with the persons on the other side. The fifth joint combat activity, I skip for now. It is mentioned in our final trial brief. It's important, because I only want to deal with meetings at this point in time, that the commander of the 3rd Corps handed down at IKM Natron further tasks. I have to apologise here because I don't find a quote. It must have escaped me. I believe it was Mr. Zilkic. Your Honours, we could provide the exact reference. I want to dwell for the last 15 minutes on the second point. Delic remained informed on combat and security. Starting with 804 of the Defence final brief, Your Honours see that the last sentence is important. The operation centre of the General Staff which was previously existed -- which previously existed in Sarajevo ceased to work after Kakanj was open, is the Defence's allegation. Your Honours, we say that the operation centre in Sarajevo functioned parallel to KM Kakanj. Mr. Delic was not cut off. There is an order from the 27th of December 1994, Exhibit 371, which says: Summary combat reports from the ARBiH staff will be delivered via the operative centre on duty in Sarajevo. If, as the Defence claims, the operation centre in Sarajevo would have stopped functioning, what is the purpose of this order in late 1994/early 1995? Obviously, this order is issued on the basis there is an operation centre. And Your Honours have seen these reports, the summary reports. I cannot list them all: Exhibit 537, 1406, 1289, Exhibit 406. I have only selected those relating to Proljece 2 and Farz. Who are the addressees? Please look for a moment on the right-hand side a very distinguished circle, and number two is the commander of the army, Your Honour. In any case, the Defence pleads, in paragraph 512, the mere fact that a document was addressed to Delic doesn't mean that he saw it. We say, Your Honours, reports on the situation in the ARBiH theatre of war - I have just shown awe couple of examples - were received as well as bulletins from Kakanj. And I will try to explain. The recipients of the bulletins - I'm switching to the Security Administration documents Your Honours, for example, Exhibit 376 - Your Honours see, again, a very distinguished circle. The president, the supreme staff commander, and it says "deputy prime minister" but it is an unrevised version. It is probably the prime minister. We are talking about the core people. We are not about random documents being sent to several corps and brigade. This is a distinguished circle, in our opinion. And the Defence is referring to Mr. Berbic who, according to the Defence's view, paragraph 512, clearly stated that: During the absence of Delic km. Kakanj, they were received by the Chief of Staff, suggesting Hadzihasanovic. We say, Your Honours, Mr. Berbic's testimony is not completely irrelevant, but let's treat it or let's deal with it to the time-period about which Mr. Berbic is competent at that talk about. And we have checked Exhibit 377. It is a compilation of some 100 bulletins -- or not bulletins, cover letters attached to bulletins going to Kakanj. When is Mr. Berbic's name showing up? The first time, as you see here, on the 27th September 1995. Farz is still ongoing, but the crime base about which we are talking in this trial is over, in the sense that the killings have occurred, Your Honours. Mr. Berbic, who was sometimes the addressee, became the addressee late in the day, as the Prosecution submits, when so to speak Farz was almost over. So the crucial bulletins, the notice bulletins we are talking about the Prosecution submits were submitted earlier. And if Your Honours look at the instructions in the cover letters, I think there is no doubt: You are required to forward the bulletin to the General Staff commander, army, General Rasim Delic, for his information. Can there be any doubt? We believe that instruction is precise. The Celibici Appeals judgement referred by Mr. Mundis this morning says: Relevant information only needs to have been provided or available to the superior. It is not required that he actually acquainted himself. What does Mr. Vuckovic who is involved in the dispatching procedure and production procedure tell Your Honours? The readers were the top officials of Bosnia Herzegovina. It is not addressed to anybody. And Mr. Softic told Your Honours. He is the chef de cabinet who is should know how crucial documents are dispatched: The operations centre in Kakanj was also subordinated to the Chief of Staff, if that's what you're thinking. And the Chief of Staff communicated with the commander. If let's just assume, theoretically, a bulletin would have ended up in the hands of Mr. Hadzihasanovic, the chef de cabinet says the Chief of Staff, as would be of course expected, is communicating with Commander Delic. The next question is: Was there a system in place for information to be reported to General Delic through the command post in Kakanj? The chef de cabinet tells Your Honours, yes, there was a system. It doesn't mean it ended up in Kakanj in a dead end. This is pages 1895, 1896, 29th of August 2007. Third point: Delic knew that the EMD was operating on the Vozuca battlefield when he ordered - that's the July Proljece 2 operation - or approved that Farz combat. The Defence starts off by denying none of the evidence in this case confirms, in paragraph 473, that Delic even knew about the participation of the detachment during combat activities in July. Flat denial, Your Honours. We say Delic knew about EMD presence at the Ozren-Vozuca battlefield when he ordered to launch combat on all fronts. Your Honours have heard that order from the 16th of July. Let's start with the bulletin. Exhibit 963, talking about the El Mujahedin Detachment. What does is say in the relevant paragraph? "It is also already known to the public that the members of this detachment in the village of Curici, in Zavidovici municipality, completely destroyed an Orthodox cemetery. Your Honours have heard it. If you look at cutout of the court binder, you see Curici on the upper left-hand corner is opposite Paljenik. We have heard a lot about the strategic importance of that feature. By April 1995, information provided to Mr. Delic. That same bulletin has a handwriting, Your Honours. And PW-13, on 6653, on the 6th of December 2007, told Your Honours: "Do you recognise the handwriting?" "Yes, this is General Delic's handwriting." So it was received and seen. Then we have -- you see the signature. It is exhibit 599. Delic's approval of the ordinary July coordination plans of the General Staff, issuing the tasks for the next month. And I have three such listed up. And you see, in section 15, Roman XV, realisation of the plan of offensive combat in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. Who is responsible? 3rd Corp and 35th Division. Then on the 4th of July, before the 16th of July order -- I note the time, Your Honour. I still have a few slides left. I endeavour my best. 4th of July, Exhibit 735. What is the information provided? 3rd Corps reports EMD tried to use their joint training with soldiers of the 328th Mountain Brigade to win them over. Who is mediating? The commander of the 35th Division and the EMD held a meeting. Your Honours, training with the 328th Mountain Brigade, 35th Division. It doesn't say the El Mujahedin Detachment is, in fact, carrying out combat on the 4th of July, but military person might infer why trainings occur. On the 10th of July, bulletin Exhibit 736. SVB of the 3rd Corps reports that members of the EMD frequently visit soldiers of adjacent units, not any units, adjacent units. Who again? The 328th Mountain Brigade. What are the soldiers of the EMD doing? When they go to the Ozren and Vozuca front, they visit. Exhibit 736. Six days before the order, launch combat on all fronts, is being issued. Your Honours, this order is in front of you, Exhibit 496. Two days later, 3rd Corps reports back to Kakanj, pursuant to your order - Your Honours have just seen it - from 16th of July. Two others are listed here: On carrying out active combat on the entire front in the basic area of the 3rd Corps, it says units of the 35th Division and, number one, in coordinate action with the EMD, carried out the necessary preparations. We expect the beginning of attack. It went to Kakanj, not to Mr. Delic at this point in time. 19th of July, a bulletin, a day later going to Mr. Delic, Exhibit 738. What is mentioned about the EMD? Six members of this unit stopped a group of girls. It's is not a war crime. We're talking about ordinary crime, but the location is interesting. They took -- it also talks about a road, Savci Krivaja. Your Honours know where that road is. On the 16th and the July this incident occurred. What are they doing, EMD? They took the members of the army towards Paljenik, one of the best fortified feature of the VRS in the area. We believe it sends a signal, Your Honours, about the presence. Three days after, an order for attack has been issued. 22nd of July, Your Honours know that bulletin. We just see it is after the fact the combat has started. Exhibit 582. What is reported? The 328th Mountain Brigade in the Vozuca -- I apologise. In the area of responsibility of the 328th Mountain Brigade, in the Vozuca battlefield, it says. It talks about joint units of the 35th Division broke through the enemy lines in the planned directions, and on that occasion liberated and villages are mentioned. The last sentence is important for Your Honours. What can be infer from the last sentence? In this action, 18 of our soldiers got killed, of our soldiers, 15 of which were members of the EMD. Isn't that an indication that six days after the 16th of July order at least one unit has lost 15 soldiers of the EMD, in that area, 328th Mountain Brigade? I want to move on. I am aware of the time, Your Honour. Please just cut me off.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not quite correctly, but I do understand that you would like to proceed in this manner. And if Mr. Neuner wants to conclude tomorrow, that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. How much more do you still have to do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I apologise a little bit because I have substantially regrouped the whole morning in order to reduce it. I'm a little bit confused. I think I'm more than two thirds through, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can reduce it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
